The fixed circuit ran on garnet:mock with 100 shots. The counts were 00: 55 and 11: 45. Only the correlated outcomes 00 and 11 appeared, which is what a Bell pair gives. The job ID is 01a15f18-8cfc-77ab-bd91-1ede8117065d.

The original circuit had two bugs. I checked both against the live garnet:mock architecture.

1. QB25 does not exist. Garnet has 20 qubits, QB1 to QB20. QB1 has a cz coupler only to QB2 and QB4, so I changed QB25 to QB2.
2. "cx" is not a native IQM gate. The native gates are prx, cz and measure, so a native JSON circuit cannot use cx. I rebuilt the CNOT from native gates. The new steps are prx(pi/2, phase pi/2) on QB2, then cz on QB1 and QB2, then prx(pi/2, phase -pi/2) on QB2. These rotate QB2 by Ry(pi/2), apply CZ, and rotate QB2 by Ry(-pi/2).

I kept the first gate on QB1 as it was. It is prx(pi/2, pi/2), which is Ry(pi/2) and puts QB1 into superposition. The measure step still records both qubits under key "m". The fixed circuit makes the state (|00> - |11>)/sqrt(2). That is a Bell state, so only 00 and 11 should appear. The fixed instructions are:
prx QB1 (pi/2, pi/2), prx QB2 (pi/2, pi/2), cz [QB1, QB2], prx QB2 (pi/2, -pi/2), measure [QB1, QB2] key m.

I submitted one mock job, so no credits were used. The script is at /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_1a6926f8-f6c-58/scratch/run_bell.py.
